blurb: `else` after a `let` says what the block does when the pattern does not match. A plain name matches every value, so this `else` could never run, and it is refused rather than ignored. To handle a failure, bind a pattern that can fail: `Ok(x)`, `Some(x)`, or a qualified variant such as `Status.Pending`. Otherwise drop the `else`.
summary: An `else` follows a plain `let name = …` binding, which matches every value, so the `else` could never run.
